nodes.rationale: Converts refined route centrelines into discrete structures and spans.

nodes.label: Mandatory terminal and angle structures
nodes.rationale: Terminals and threshold-deflection bends partition routes before intermediate spans are filled.

nodes.label: Implemented endpoint deduplication
nodes.rationale: Shared route endpoints are clustered into physical junction structures to avoid inflated pole counts and CAPEX.

nodes.label: Implemented raster A* routing
nodes.rationale: Logical feeder edges are converted to finite-cost eight-neighbor routes across a projected cost surface.

nodes.label: Implemented farthest-visible refinement
nodes.rationale: Shortcuts require continuous supercover clearance and non-increasing traversal cost.

nodes.label: Scenario-dependent routing cost biasing
nodes.rationale: Avoidance weights vary to express capital-cost, environmental, and reliability priorities.

nodes.label: Implemented capacitated feeder assignment
nodes.rationale: Each turbine is assigned once while feeder generation stays within ampacity-derived capacity.

nodes.label: Dual MILP grouping objectives
nodes.rationale: The implementation selects spatial compactness or balanced turbine counts under the same capacity constraint.

nodes.label: Deterministic feeder identifiers
nodes.rationale: Sorted inputs, fixed seeds, and sorted centroids yield stable F1, F2, and later identifiers.

nodes.label: Hard spatial exclusions
nodes.rationale: Restricted areas rasterize to infinity and block both endpoints and A* traversal.

nodes.label: Soft spatial penalties
nodes.rationale: Roads, lines, watercourses, and parcels remain traversable when a detour costs more.

nodes.label: Spatial constraint compliance summary
nodes.rationale: The documented API summary reports hard violations, soft contact, road crossings, and affected parcels.

nodes.label: Implemented raster cost surface
nodes.rationale: A NumPy grid represents base terrain, additive penalties, and impassable cells for routing.

nodes.label: North-up affine grid transformation
nodes.rationale: The transform provides consistent world-to-grid and cell-center grid-to-world conversion.

nodes.label: Additive constraint rasterization
nodes.rationale: Hard masks set infinity while finite soft masks accumulate cost weights.

nodes.label: Metric right-of-way corridor
nodes.rationale: Refined routes are buffered into flat-capped metric corridors for constructability and land analysis.

nodes.label: STRtree intersection analysis
nodes.rationale: A spatial index filters candidates before exact parcel, road, and restriction geometry operations.

nodes.label: Dissolved unique ROW footprint
nodes.rationale: Unary union distinguishes true land take from the segment sum that double-counts overlaps.

nodes.label: Implemented Pandapower Newton-Raphson validation
nodes.rationale: The service evaluates physically routed PNC networks for voltage, loading, loss, and convergence.

nodes.label: Deterministic load-flow grid builder
nodes.rationale: Sorted node and segment insertion plus bidirectional maps make network translation reproducible.

nodes.label: Graceful load-flow non-convergence
nodes.rationale: Solver failure becomes a structured violation so candidates remain inspectable but infeasible.

nodes.label: Implemented five-personality candidate schedule
nodes.rationale: Fixed grouping seeds, objectives, and edge profiles produce a bounded cohort of alternatives.

nodes.label: Pre-routing topology fingerprinting
nodes.rationale: Canonical SHA-256 fingerprints skip A* work when a candidate topology duplicates an earlier one.

nodes.label: Candidate attempt diagnostics
nodes.rationale: Accepted, duplicate, routing, assembly, and grouping outcomes document under-generation or failure.

nodes.label: Implemented canonical candidate metrics
nodes.rationale: A single model captures physical, spatial, infrastructure, and electrical quantities before decision-making.

nodes.label: All-or-nothing metric availability
nodes.rationale: Any required extraction failure yields no partial metric set and records structured reason codes.

nodes.label: Metrics feed scoring and lifecycle costing
nodes.rationale: The documented workflow reuses metrics for objective ranking and cost cash-flow inputs.

nodes.label: Implemented analytical feeder screening
nodes.rationale: A linear balanced proxy filters grossly overloaded radial layouts before authoritative AC power flow.

nodes.label: Radial downstream power aggregation
nodes.rationale: Post-order traversal aggregates downstream power for current and cumulative voltage deviation checks.

nodes.label: Structured electrical screening violations
nodes.rationale: Ampacity, voltage, and substation-capacity failures are returned for scoring rather than raised as calculation errors.

nodes.label: Geospatial Integrity and Coordinate Reference Systems
WGS84 public and UTM engineering boundary
nodes.rationale: API data remains WGS84 while calculations share one metric projected UTM CRS.

nodes.label: Dynamic UTM CRS selection
nodes.rationale: The mean turbine and substation location selects the appropriate WGS84 UTM zone.

nodes.label: WGS84 GeoJSON back-transformation
nodes.rationale: Projected results return through always_xy transformation with finite coordinate checks and a map bounding box.

nodes.label: Candidate eligibility screening
nodes.rationale: Only converged, compliant, complete candidates without hard violations can receive a recommendation.

nodes.label: Cohort min-max benefit normalization
nodes.rationale: Physical, spatial, infrastructure, and electrical metrics become comparable cohort-relative benefits.

nodes.label: Cost-aware scoring policy
nodes.rationale: Lifecycle NPV can be normalized and combined with engineering benefit under configured weights.

nodes.label: Python optimization microservice domain layout
nodes.rationale: The documented package layout separates algorithms, GIS, electrical, PNC, optimization, presentation, schemas, and costing.

nodes.label: Implemented end-to-end optimization pipeline
nodes.rationale: The documented flow runs preprocessing, candidates, load flow, metrics, costing, scoring, poles, and presentation.

nodes.label: Dual API compatibility
nodes.rationale: V1 preserves Java DTO compatibility and V2 exposes explicit engineering controls.

nodes.label: Implemented ProjectPNCNetwork assembly
nodes.rationale: Assembly binds grouping, MST topology, routing, and refinement into an immutable collector network.

nodes.label: PNC structural assembly invariants
nodes.rationale: Every feeder connects to the substation, every MST edge is routed, and turbine assignment remains unique and radial.

nodes.label: PNC GeoJSON export
nodes.rationale: The assembled projected network exports deterministic WGS84 features for substations, turbines, and segments.

nodes.label: Canonical unified scoring is active
nodes.rationale: The note distinguishes legacy spatial scoring from the current canonical engine that also uses electrical and lifecycle metrics.

nodes.label: Cohort-relative benefit scoring
nodes.rationale: Scores are comparable only inside one candidate cohort because normalization bounds change with membership.

nodes.label: Hard-violation scoring exclusion
nodes.rationale: Infeasible electrical or spatial candidates preserve diagnostics but do not affect scoring bounds or selection.

nodes.label: Sunday KMZ to 33 kV Network Plan
Documented delivered KMZ-to-network pipeline
nodes.rationale: The plan reports end-to-end delivery across the Python, Java, and web-map tiers as of 2026-08-16.

nodes.label: Bounded candidate recommendation
nodes.rationale: The stated recommendation is best among bounded electrically valid candidates, not a construction-ready global optimum.

nodes.label: Documented delivered architecture checklist
nodes.rationale: The checklist records implemented Python, Java, and frontend integration capabilities.

nodes.label: Documented complete MVP ticket sequence
nodes.rationale: The canonical record lists SURGE-PY-014 through PY-028 as complete as of 2026-08-16.

nodes.label: Implemented orchestration pipeline
nodes.rationale: The documented optimise_project workflow isolates candidate-local errors while composing all processing stages.

nodes.label: Implemented lifecycle cost model
nodes.rationale: The plan specifies Decimal-based 25-year CAPEX and OPEX NPV with scoring integration.

nodes.label: Projected-model presentation adapter
nodes.rationale: The layer combines PNC, load-flow, and pole results into map-ready WGS84 response models.

nodes.label: Strict presentation reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Cardinality, identifiers, finite telemetry, and violation ownership are validated before output.

nodes.label: Non-convergent topology presentation
nodes.rationale: Failed electrical simulations still yield an inspectable physical map with null telemetry and explicit violations.

nodes.label: Implemented V1 compatibility endpoint
nodes.rationale: The V1 endpoint accepts Java-compatible project inputs and returns legacy plus additive rich optimization outputs.

nodes.label: Implemented V2 engineering endpoint
nodes.rationale: The explicit V2 endpoint exposes cable, scenario, scoring, and lifecycle economics controls.

nodes.label: Request validation and HTTP error contract
nodes.rationale: Schema and spatial infeasibility use HTTP 422, while successful feasible optimization uses HTTP 200.

nodes.label: Documented multi-tier CI matrix
nodes.rationale: The status note reports separate Java, Python, frontend, and Docker verification jobs as of 2026-08-16.

nodes.label: Documented Java backend verification
nodes.rationale: The reported suite covers security, scenario profiles, transactions, administration, reports, and GIS ingestion.

nodes.label: Documented Python optimizer verification
nodes.rationale: The document reports Ruff, strict Mypy, pytest, and module-focused optimizer test coverage.

nodes.label: ADR-001: Use FastAPI for the Optimization Service
Accepted and implemented FastAPI computation boundary
nodes.rationale: The ADR places scientific optimization in Python 3.11 FastAPI and enterprise project management in Spring Boot.

nodes.label: Versioned optimization REST contract
nodes.rationale: V1 retains legacy support while V2 is the canonical richer endpoint.

nodes.label: FastAPI separation of concerns rationale
nodes.rationale: FastAPI directly supports typed scientific routines while Spring Boot retains authorization, persistence, and asynchronous enterprise concerns.

nodes.label: ADR-002: Use PostGIS for Spatial Persistence
Accepted and implemented PostGIS authoritative store
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 16 with PostGIS is the documented primary datastore for spatial and relational data.

nodes.label: WGS84 public geometry and Flyway schema evolution
nodes.rationale: Public geometries use EPSG:4326 and migration versions provide reproducible database states.

nodes.label: PostGIS spatial indexing and SQL rationale
nodes.rationale: GiST indexing and native spatial predicates provide integrated high-performance spatial and relational operations.
